rows.evidence: unchanged since 4051c1a (git diff checked); round-23 evidence: Re-derived: by stationarity T Var(dbar) = T^-1 sum_{s,t} gamma(t - s) = sum_{|h| < T} (1 - |h|/T) gamma(h). rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L03.html Lemma 2.3 (line 102) and its proof; card S7-c217
rows.evidence: unchanged since 4051c1a (git diff checked); round-23 evidence: Re-derived. (a) p_(k) <= kq/m iff at least k p-values are <= kq/m: if p_(k) <= kq/m then p_(1..k) are all <= kq/m, so N(k) >= k; if N(k) >= k then the k-th smallest is <= kq/m. Hence R = max{k : N(k) >= k}. (b) If R >= 1, a rejected H_i has p_i <= p_(R) <= Rq/m. Conversely, if p_i <= Rq/m but p_i = p_(j) with j > R, then p_(j) <= Rq/m <= jq/m, so N(j) >= j, contradicting the maximality of R; the zero case is handled (N(1) >= 1 forces R >= 1). (c) Raising a p-value can only lower each N(k), so the largest k with N(k) >= k cannot increase. Numerical spot check (scratch py/spotchecks_r12.py): for 2,000 random p-vectors (m = 10, q = 0.05, mixed scales) the BH rejection set equals {i : p_i <= R q/m} with R = max{k : N(k) >= k} (0 violations), and R does not increase when one randomly chosen p-value is raised (0 violations). Ties: the proof uses the k-th smallest p-value, so ties do not change the count.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L03.html Proposition 5.3 (line 281) and its proof; card S7-c218
rows.evidence: unchanged since 4051c1a (git diff checked); round-23 evidence: Re-derived for rho in [0,1). Given z_i = t, the joint Gaussian (W, z_i) gives W | z_i = t ~ N(sqrt(rho)(t - mu_i), 1 - rho), stochastically increasing in t for rho >= 0 (the constant case rho = 0 is trivially monotone). The other coordinates are z_j = sqrt(rho) W + sqrt(1-rho) eps_j + mu_j with eps_j independent of (W, z_i), so P(z in D' | z_i = t) = E[g(W) | z_i = t], g non-increasing for a decreasing D' (translating all z_j by a common amount). Hence t -> P(z in D' | z_i = t) is non-increasing, which is PRDS (Definition 5.1) on every subset. Numerical spot check (scratch py/spotchecks_r12.py, Monte Carlo 600,000 draws, rho = 0.5, m = 3, D = {p_2 >= 1/2, p_3 >= 1/2}, an increasing set in p-space): P(D | z_1 near t) falls from 0.556 at t = -1 to 0.033 at t = 2 (non-increasing in t), and P(D | p_1 near u) rises from 0.054 at u = 0.05 to 0.708 at u = 0.95 (non-decreasing in u): the PRDS inequality holds in the numerical check. (An earlier attempt used the z-increasing set {z_2 > 0, z_3 > 0}; that set is not an increasing set of p-values, so it was discarded.)

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L04.html line 365 (section 6, the T span: 'Step 2 of Definition 4.1 subtracts each strategy's own sample mean ... never more')
rows.evidence: unchanged since 4051c1a (git diff checked); round-23 evidence: Re-derived from Definition 4.1 (L04.html lines 268–275: V_K = max_k sqrt(T) dbar_k; V*_{K,j} = max_k sqrt(T)(dbar*_{k,j} - dbar_k) with one index sequence per draw shared by all strategies; p-hat = mean_j 1{V*_{K,j} >= V_K}). (a) Adding any strategy adds one term to each maximum: V*_{K+1,j} = max(V*_{K,j}, term_j) >= V*_{K,j} for every draw j. (b) If its statistic s = sqrt(T) dbar_{K+1} is not the largest (s <= V_K), then V_{K+1} = V_K. (c) Hence with the same draws p-hat can only rise, and rejection at alpha (p-hat <= alpha) can only be lost. Numerical check of (a)–(c) with the Definition 4.1 procedure, seed 20261020, 300 trials, T = 120, B = 400, K from 2 to 7 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify22h-L03-L04/derive/rc_pathwise_check.py, output /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify22h-L03-L04/derive/rc_pathwise_check.out): non-largest additions 210: V_K unchanged in 210 of 210; V*_(K+1,j) >= V*_(K,j) for every draw in all 300 trials (0 violations); p-hat fell in 0 of 210. Control (d): when the added statistic is the largest, p-hat fell in 74 of 90 trials, so the claim needs the 'not the largest' condition. The span's clause 'such a poor alternative can make the Reality Check reject less often, never more' refers, through 'such', to a strategy whose statistic is not the largest; read pathwise (same data and draws) it is exactly (a)–(c). rows.check: 2.3-grade and 2.4-math (Roquain span, grade T with locator 'Theorem 2.5 (arXiv v3, 2020)')
rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L03.html line 409: Roquain and Verzelen show that an estimated null cannot always stand in for the true one: when the nulls are Gaussian with unknown mean and variance, a procedure that asymptotically matches Benjamini-Hochberg run with the true null exists if and only if the number of false nulls is of order less than N/log N, where N is the number of tests
rows.evidence: unchanged since 4051c1a (git diff checked); round-23 evidence: Grade: T is the right grade for a result the paper proves with a precisely named theorem (BLUEPRINT section 3: 'proved on the page, or with a precisely cited proof'); the cited proofs are in the arXiv v3 PDF (dl/roquain_arxiv_v3/roquain_v3.txt). Theorem 2.5 (arXiv v3, p. 12 of the paper; image crop dl/roquain_arxiv_v3/thm25-11.png, 200 dpi, read): '(i) for a sparsity k_n >> n/log(n), there exists no (sequence of) AMO procedure that is AMO; (ii) for a sparsity k_n << n/log(n), the sequence of plug-in BH procedure (BH_alpha(theta~, sigma~)) is AMO, for the scaling (theta~, sigma~) given by standard robust estimators (13).' Section 2.7.2 restates it as dense (k_n >> n/log n) and sparse (k_n << n/log n) regimes. Attribution: 'Gaussian with an unknown rescaling parameters (mean and variance) and the alternative distribution is let arbitrary' (abstract) matches 'Gaussian nulls with unknown mean and variance'; the alternative is unrestricted in the paper, which the span does not say (scope is narrower than the paper, not wider; non-blocking). AMO (Definition 2.2) is 'asymptotically mimicking the oracle BH procedure': the span's 'asymptotically matches Benjamini-Hochberg run with the true null' is right. The 'if and only if ... of order less than N/log N' is the abstract's main-result sentence; at the level of orders it is proved: Theorem 3.1 (non-asymptotic lower bound: no procedure with FDR <= c3 is AMO when k2 >= c2 n log(2/alpha)(1+log(k2/k1))/log n) and Theorem 3.2 (plug-in BH is AMO when eta = c2 log(n/alpha)(k/n) v n^(-1/6) <= 0.05, i.e. k of order n/log n or below), so the boundary is order n/log n with constants. Theorem 2.5 itself is stated with >> and <<, so the locator should read 'Theorem 2.5; Theorems 3.1-3.2 (order-level constants)'. That is a precision suggestion, not a failure. Symbols: N is registered as local (notation/notation.json 'about': N is defined in each lesson), and the span defines it in the same sentence. Published-version numbering not verified (R22-cite-roquain2022false).
